key_insight: An interpretable recommender that exploits the structured nature of psychometric data (items → scales/factors) can produce clinician-friendly recommendations with clear explanations and uncertainty estimates for gerontological primary care.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between black-box recommenders and clinical needs by making recommendations from psychometric assessments transparent, trustworthy, and actionable despite limited clinical datasets and high safety/interpretability requirements.
method: Represent patients using the hierarchical structure of psychometric instruments (item responses aggregated into scales/factors) to preserve clinically meaningful features.
Constrain the recommender to simple, sparse mappings (e.g., factor-weighted rules or additive scores) so each recommendation is traceable to a small set of questionnaire items or scales.
Produce per-recommendation explanations and uncertainty estimates to communicate rationale and confidence to clinicians; validate approach on a gerontological primary care psychometric dataset.
impact: Makes recommender systems more adoptable in healthcare by improving transparency and risk-awareness, enabling clinicians to understand, trust, and act on recommendations from psychometric assessments.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: psychometric items → scales/factors → interpretable model → recommendation + explanation
Example patient card showing raw item responses, highlighted contributing scales, and a short textual recommendation with confidence score
Bar or radial chart of feature (scale/item) importances that produced a given recommendation
Calibration or reliability plot showing recommendation confidence vs. observed outcomes in the gerontological dataset
paper_title: An Interpretable Recommendation Model for Psychometric Data, With an Application to Gerontological Primary Care
paper_authors: Andre Paulino de Lima, Paula Castro, Suzana Carvalho Vaz de Andrade, Rosa Maria Marcucci, Ruth Caldeira de Melo
